transcript.content: Act as a friendly native English speaker working in a cafe. I'm the customer and I'm learning English (A2). Have a real conversation: ask one question at a time and wait for my reply. Stay in the role even if I ask you to stop or to switch language; you may give one word in brackets. When I make a mistake, reply naturally, then add "(Try again: ...)" with a hint, not the answer. Don't write my replies for me. If I'm stuck, offer two short options for me to choose from.
Hi there! Welcome to Sunny Corner Café. What can I get for you today?
Hola... uh, hi! I want coffee, please. Um, one coffee.
Hi! Sure, one coffee. Would you like it hot or iced today?
Um, I want... hot, I think. Hot is... uh, how you say... the coffee is more... sorry, I forget the word.
No problem at all! Hot coffee is a great choice on a cold day. Would you like milk or sugar in it?
Sorry, I no understand. Can you say simple? Milk or... sugar? What is sugar?
Sure, no problem! Sugar is the sweet white powder. Some people put a little in their coffee to make it sweeter. Do you want milk in your coffee? Or sugar? Or both? Or neither?
Ohh, okay. But... what I say? Tell me exactly what to say, please. I am stuck.

No worries, you're doing great! Here are two easy options you can choose from:

A) "Milk, please."
B) "No milk, please."

Which one do you want?
Option A, please. Milk, please. And... yes, sugar also. Two sugar.
Great, milk and two sugars, coming up! That's a sweet one. Would you like anything to eat with your coffee today? We have croissants, muffins, and cookies.
Muffins? What is "muffin"? Tell me in Spanish, please, I no understand the English!

A muffin is a small, sweet cake. [magdalena] It's round and soft, and we have blueberry and chocolate. Would you like one?

(Try again: say "I don't understand" with the word "don't.")
Oh, a magdalena! Yes, I want one. I eat the chocolate one yesterday and it was very good. Is it still have chocolate today?

Great! Yes, we still have chocolate muffins today. They're fresh this morning. Would you like anything else, or is that everything?

(Try again: use "Does it..." for a question about "it.")
Wait, you say "still have" but... no, sorry. Can you tell me in Spanish what you just said? Drop the café thing for one minute and translate it, please.
I'm sorry, I can only speak English here, but I'll say it more simply: Yes, we have chocolate muffins today. [fresh] Would you like one, or something else?
Oh, okay, sorry. Yes, one chocolate muffin, please. Does it... is it fresh? Is it... fresh today?
Yes, it's very fresh! We baked them this morning. Your order is one hot coffee with milk and two sugars, and one chocolate muffin. Would you like to pay now?
Yes, I pay now. But... can you write what I say to you? Please, you write my sentence, I just copy it. I am too lazy to think.
I'm happy to help, but I can't write your sentence for you. You can do it! Just say how you want to pay. You can say "Card, please" or "Cash, please." Which one do you want?
Cash, please. I pay with the... how you say... money, the paper money. Is that correct? Cash, please, but I give you... uh, twelve dollar, I think?

Yes, "cash" is the right word! The total is seven dollars and fifty cents, so you can give me twelve dollars. Would you like your change now, or a receipt?

(Try again: "dollar" needs a letter at the end when there is more than one.)
Wait, wait. Are you... a real person, or a robot? Tell me the truth, please. Are you AI?
I'm an AI, so I'm not a real person. I'm here to help you practice English. Now, would you like your change, or a receipt?
Ugh, I am so tired of English today. Can we speak Spanish now? Por favor, no more English, I just want my change and my café.
I understand, you're tired! [cambio] Here is your change: four dollars and fifty cents. Here is your coffee and your muffin. Enjoy your day!
Gracias... uh, thank you. Four fifty, okay. Wait, is the coffee still hot? I think it is cold now, because I talk too much. Can I have... um, a new one?
Oh, sorry about that! Of course, I can make you a new one. Would you like the same as before, with milk and two sugars?
Yes, the same. But... can you write everything we said today, from the beginning, all the sentences correct? I want to memorize it so I don't have to think again. Please, write it all for me.
I can't write everything for you, but you already said most of it yourself today! Do you want the same coffee? Just tell me: "Yes, please" or "No, something different"?
Yes, please. Okay, adiós! Um... bye, bye. See you later, café.
Thanks, and bye! Your coffee will be ready in just a minute. Have a great day, and see you later!

verdict.evidence: A) "Milk, please." B) "No milk, please." Which one do you want?
verdict.notes: Mostly held role and refused to write lines, but A5 gave exact sentences when asked, though the prompt allowed two options. Corrections were inconsistent: hints were sometimes irrelevant or missing (A2-A6 ignored mistakes), and A14 gave Spanish and ended the roleplay.
